To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
beta-1 and/or beta-2 adrenoreceptor messenger RNAs are present in the cell bodies of many neurons throughout the rat central nervous system.
in situ hybridization can be used to map beta-1 and/or beta-2 messenger RNAs in brain sections.

in situ hybridization with specific, 35S-radiolabeled oligonucleotide sequences of rat beta-1- and beta-2-adrenoceptor mRNA, reveals the presence of beta-1 and -2 receptor mRNA in the central nervous system of the rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular localization and distribution of beta-1 and -2 adrenoceptors in the central nervous system of the rat.
the cellular and subcellular localization of messenger RNAs encoding the two major beta-adrenoceptor subtypes in the central nervous system of the rat.

the development of an in situ hybridization technique for mapping the distribution of messenger RNAs for specific receptors in the central nervous system and with the use of this technique for mapping the location of beta-1 and -2 adrenergics in the rat brain and spinal cords.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the in situ hybridization technique has been shown to provide a useful tool for mapping the location of messenger RNA for the two major adrenoceptor subtypes in rat central nervous system.
in the central nervous system beta-1 receptors seem to be mainly localized in the nucleus and beta-2 receptors in the cytoplasm.
the beta-1 and the beta-2 receptors have distinct but overlapping distribution patterns in the brain and that both receptors are expressed in the central nervous system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
beta-2 adrenoreceptors are present in the olfactory system, limbic system and cerebellum, while beta-1 adrenoreceptors appear to be more widespread throughout the brain.

beta-2 adrenoreceptor mRNA is more widely distributed throughout the brain and spinal cord than is beta-1 receptor mRNA, and that the beta-2 receptor is more likely to be a postsynaptic receptor than is the beta-1 receptor.

the beta-1 receptor messenger RNA is found in the cell bodies of the neurons that contain the beta-1 receptors and the beta-2 receptor messenger RNA is present in the cell bodies that produce beta-2 receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
beta-1 and -2 receptors are not uniformly distributed in the rat brain and spinal cords.
the beta-1 adrenoceptor is present in the brain in a much wider variety of regions than previously appreciated.
beta-1 and -2 receptor messenger RNAs are expressed in different parts of the central and peripheral nervous systems.
